home.heroSubtitle: EduAIR provides a range of innovative AI teaching kits and courses
home.cardDescription: EduAIR (愛動智) is a Hong Kong non-profit spun out of a CUHK research team. We build AI teaching kits, run on-site workshops, and train teachers — bilingual and curriculum-mapped.
home.aboutTitle: Comprehensive AI Education Support for Schools
home.aboutBody: EduAIR is building a shared learning platform offering a range of services that help students get to grips with AI and STEAM — understanding and applying that knowledge more deeply through hands-on, interactive learning that sparks curiosity and creativity.
home.kitsIntro: EduAIR's own iPort, iCar, iShare and iTrain platforms let students put AI and AIoT concepts into practice, building a real AI learning experience.

kits.name: iCar
kits.subtitle: AI Smart Car Teaching Kit
kits.body: iCar is an AI smart car kit designed for primary and secondary schools. Students program the car to complete various tasks, learning the basic principles of AI perception, decision-making and action.

kits.name: iPort
kits.subtitle: AIoT Maker Education Kit
kits.body: iPort is EduAIR's flagship AIoT teaching kit, integrating a range of sensors, actuators and AI modules so students can put AIoT concepts into practice and complete real smart-device projects.

kits.name: iShare
kits.subtitle: AI Collaborative Learning Platform
kits.body: iShare is EduAIR's AI collaborative learning platform, letting students complete AI projects together in the cloud, share their results, and build an AI learning community.

about.heroTitle: We build the AI lessons we wished we'd had in the classroom.
about.heroBody: EduAIR (愛動智教育系統) is a Hong Kong non-profit edtech company designing AI and STEAM teaching kits, workshops, and teacher training for primary and secondary schools.
about.aboutBody: EduAIR is a non-profit organisation dedicated to promoting AI education in Hong Kong, helping young people build AI/STEAM skills, and supporting them in pursuing their goals in related fields.

storyChapters.label: ORIGIN
storyChapters.heading: Backed by CUHK researchers
storyChapters.body: EduAIR Systems Limited (愛動智) is a non-profit started with backing from a CUHK innovation seed fund, built around a research team already working on AI/STEAM education.

storyChapters.label: THE IDEA
storyChapters.heading: Turning AI into a teachable curriculum
storyChapters.body: The founding team broke AI topics into a structured, classroom-ready course — one that didn't require a computer science background to teach or to learn from.

storyChapters.label: WHERE IT STANDS
storyChapters.heading: In more than 50% of HK's secondary schools
storyChapters.body: That course, and the iCar kit built around it, is now used by more than half of Hong Kong's secondary schools for AI teaching activities.

about.teamTitle: Supported and built up by a CUHK research team
about.teamBody: EduAIR is made up of researchers with deep experience in technology education. Their expertise drives our mission to advance AI/STEAM education in Hong Kong.

icar.intro: iCar is developed by the research team at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK). It is an AI teaching kit specifically designed for junior secondary school students, able to perform several interesting experiments to learn AI using Blockly programming. More than half of local secondary schools are utilizing iCar to conduct AI teaching activities.

howToUse.title: MakeCode Blockly Programming
howToUse.body: Program iCar visually using drag-and-drop Blockly blocks — no typed code required.

howToUse.title: Mobile Bluetooth Control
howToUse.body: Control iCar directly from a phone over Bluetooth using the companion app.

howToUse.title: Infrared Remote Control
howToUse.body: Drive iCar manually with a standard infrared remote for quick, code-free demos.

experiments.title: Moral Dilemma
experiments.description: When the braking function of a self-driving car fails, and it can only turn left or right. Regardless of which route it chooses, the vehicle will encounter pedestrians — on one side, kids, and on the other, the elderly. What should the autonomous car do, and what roles do humans and AI play in that decision? Students experiment with iCar to find out.
questions: What machine learning method does iCar use?
When collecting data, what should we pay attention to, and why?
Besides evading kids and evading elderlies, does iCar have a third option?

experiments.title: Face Following
experiments.description: Why can self-driving cars recognize faces and follow a specified face? How does a self-driving car learn this skill? Students experiment with iCar to find out.
questions: How does iCar learn to recognize specific faces?
Does iCar's performance change when recognizing the same face from different angles, and why?
What are the benefits and limitations of this technology in real-life situations?

experiments.title: Line Tracking
experiments.description: Self-driving cars can move based on various colored lines, both dashed and solid, to follow the correct path. How is this achieved? Students experiment with iCar to find out.
questions: Is there a difference in iCar's performance when following hand-drawn lines versus printed lines?
Does the thickness, size or shape of the lines affect iCar's movement?
What are real-life applications of line-tracking technology?

experiments.title: Food Delivery
experiments.description: Reasoning is the process of deciding what action to take to complete a task, based on the information at hand — divided into three levels: skill-based, rule-based, and knowledge-based. The Food Delivery experiment shows behaviour under each reasoning level: students choose different delivery locations and observe how iCar's route choice changes.

reasoningVideos.label: Skill-based Reasoning
reasoningVideos.caption: Uses the most straightforward method to finish the task.

reasoningVideos.label: Rule-based Reasoning
reasoningVideos.caption: Makes decisions based on learned patterns and executes them.

reasoningVideos.label: Knowledge-based Reasoning
reasoningVideos.caption: Applies machine learning to figure out the best solution.

iport.intro: iPort is an AI education toolkit developed by the CUHK team. With just three simple steps, students can create their own AI projects, encouraging creative learning in AI. By training an AI model on the no-code iTrain platform and connecting STEM components, iPort can control its outputs based on AI classification results — turning a project into a working AIoT application.
steps: Train an AI model and generate a link
Upload the model to the programming platform

experiments.title: Stranger Alert System
experiments.description: Train an AI image recognition model to detect whether someone is present at a restricted area gate. Through the iPort programming platform, simple configuration can trigger safety warnings, sound alerts, and lighting effects — reminding unauthorized individuals to leave whenever someone passes through.
questions: Is it possible to allow only authorized individuals through the gate, instead of alerting for anyone who passes?
Why might the alarm trigger after dark, and how can false triggers be avoided?
If the "someone is present" model is trained only on photos of one classmate, is that enough data to reliably detect a person?

experiments.title: Gesture-controlled Car
experiments.description: After training a gesture recognition model of your choice, students control the movement of a car through gestures using the camera. The wireless control distance can reach up to 50 meters in an open environment — try a competition to see whose car can exit a maze the fastest.
questions: What are the differences between image-recognition gesture control and traditional gesture-recognition techniques?
How can data collection be optimized to improve control of the car?

experiments.title: Audio-controlled Light Switch
experiments.description: iPort's switch-box accessory simulates realistic pushing and pulling movements. For individuals with mobility challenges, training a sound recognition model enables easy control of switches at home using simple voice commands — the wireless control distance can reach up to 15 meters even indoors with obstacles.
questions: How can the accuracy of voice control be improved?
Noise may affect voice recognition accuracy and cause false triggers — how can we reduce the impact of noise?

faq.question: What age groups do EduAIR's kits and courses suit?
faq.answer: iCar is built for junior secondary students, iPort needs no coding background so it suits younger students too, and iShare's resources span primary through senior secondary.

faq.question: Do our teachers need a coding background to run a workshop?
faq.answer: No. iPort requires no coding at all, and our on-site workshops include teacher training so your staff can run sessions independently afterward.

faq.question: Can EduAIR help us apply for funding?
faq.answer: Yes — we help schools prepare applications for schemes such as the Secondary School IT Innovation Lab and other STEAM-related funding.

faq.question: How do we book an on-site workshop?
faq.answer: Get in touch through our contact page or call +852 6437 3924 — most enquiries receive a proposal within two working days.

faq.question: Are teaching materials available in both Chinese and English?
faq.answer: Yes, most iCar lesson materials are available as separate Chinese and English downloads.

faq.question: Is EduAIR a registered organisation?
faq.answer: Yes — EduAIR Systems Limited is a registered charity in Hong Kong, registration no. 91/18516.
